observations: body L1-L3, L25-L28: the head of the commentary on chapter 42 is set in small capitals; the dashes after «a)» and «b)» and before «Schiaparelli» (L25) measure 10.0 to 10.1 pt, the dash of «33—pag.» (L26) 9.3 pt; «5–11» (L2), «38–40» and «al–Battānī» (L28) have long dashes (5.3 pt). Heavy brackets open Schiaparelli's additions in L3 and L27 and close the first in L25; the second goes on to p. 274.

body L3-L5: 5° 1′ and 7° 40′ are the greatest equations of the anomaly at the syzygies and at the quadratures, the apparent radius of the epicycle, 5;15 parts, seen from 60 parts and from 60 − 2 × 10;19 = 39;22 parts; their difference is 2° 39′ = 159′, and 5° 1′ = 301′.

body L8-L9, L13: the hourly motion in anomaly, 13° 3′ 54″ a day, is 32′ 40″ an hour, about 33′. The distance of the centre of the epicycle, 60 parts, is 11.4 times its radius, 5;15 parts; the print takes twelve times, which gives 33′ : 12 = 165″. In L13, 165″ · 2/180 = 33″/18, and 33 · 159 = 5247, 18 · 301 = 5418: the coefficient is 0.968.

body L22-L23: the small chapter H of al-Battānī (p. 150, L24-L30 of the translation) subtracts the minutes when the corrected anomaly lies from 0° to 95° or from 265° to 360°, and adds them from 95° to 265°.

body L28, L33-L34: the precept of p. 93, L38-L40 of the translation adds 1/6 + 1/8 = 7/24 of the difference to the anomaly when the degrees of the Sun exceed those of the Moon. The mean synodic motion, 12° 11′ 27″ a day (p. 267), is 30′ 29″ an hour, 1° in 1 h 58 min.
body L35: «media» at the beginning of the line is set in bold italic, heavier than the italic «excedet»; kept as printed.
body L37-L38: specks stand before «Sit» (L37), above the space between «cfr.» and «p.» (L38) and above the stop after «EO» (L38); they are not punctuation.
